name: OpenSearch
description: Protects against destructive OpenSearch REST API operations and AWS CLI domain deletions.

destructive_patterns.name: os-curl-delete-doc
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X DELETE against /_doc deletes a document from OpenSearch.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting individual documents removes them from search results immediately. \ While less destructive than bulk operations, this can affect applications \ expecting the document to exist.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the document first to verify content \ - Use _update API to mark as deleted instead \ - Ensure document ID is correct before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: os-curl-delete-by-query
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X POST to _delete_by_query deletes documents matching the query.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The _delete_by_query endpoint can delete large numbers of documents at once. \ A poorly constructed query can remove more data than intended. This operation \ cannot be easily undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use _search with same query first to preview matches \ - Add conflicts=abort to stop on version conflicts \ - Use scroll_size to process in smaller batches

destructive_patterns.name: os-curl-close-index
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X POST to _close closes an index, making it unavailable for reads/writes.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Closing an index makes it completely unavailable for search and indexing. \ Applications will receive errors until the index is reopened. Using _all or * \ can close all indices at once.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Check index status with _cat/indices first \ - Use specific index names instead of wildcards \ - Verify no active applications depend on the index

destructive_patterns.name: os-curl-delete-index
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X DELETE against an OpenSearch index (or _all/*) deletes data permanently.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an OpenSearch index permanently removes all documents, mappings, and \ settings. Using _all or * patterns can delete multiple indices at once. This \ action cannot be undone without restoring from a snapshot.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - _cat/indices: List indices before deletion \ - Create a snapshot before deleting \ - Close the index first if just archiving

destructive_patterns.name: aws-opensearch-delete-domain
destructive_patterns.description: aws opensearch delete-domain permanently deletes an OpenSearch domain.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an OpenSearch domain removes the entire cluster including all indices, \ data, and configuration. This is irreversible and affects all applications using \ the domain. Automated snapshots may also be deleted.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws opensearch describe-domain: Review domain configuration \ - Create a manual snapshot before deletion \ - Export data to S3 for long-term retention

destructive_patterns.name: aws-opensearch-delete-inbound-connection
destructive_patterns.description: aws opensearch delete-inbound-connection removes an OpenSearch connection.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an inbound connection removes cross-cluster connectivity. Applications \ performing cross-cluster searches or replication will fail. The connection must \ be re-established from the source domain.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - List connections to understand dependencies \ - Verify no active cross-cluster operations \ - Update applications to use alternative data sources

destructive_patterns.name: aws-opensearch-delete-outbound-connection
destructive_patterns.description: aws opensearch delete-outbound-connection removes an OpenSearch connection.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an outbound connection removes cross-cluster connectivity from this \ domain. Any cross-cluster searches or replication to other domains will fail. \ Re-establishing requires a new connection request.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - List connections to understand what will be affected \ - Coordinate with teams using connected domains \ - Test connection removal in a non-production environment

destructive_patterns.name: aws-opensearch-delete-package
destructive_patterns.description: aws opensearch delete-package removes an OpenSearch package.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a package removes custom plugins, dictionaries, or scripts. Domains \ using this package may experience errors or degraded functionality. The package \ must be re-uploaded if needed again.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - List domains using this package first \ - Dissociate package from domains before deletion \ - Keep a copy of package contents for recovery
